messages:
ops-bot: Automated alert: hosted-inference gateway 5xx spike detected in us-west (us-west-2). window=5m, 5xx_rate=8.7%, p95_latency=2300ms, affected_zones=[us-west-2a, us-west-2b]

sophia (oncall): Copy. I see increased 502/504 from api-gateway -> runtime pool. Paging infra + neteng. Customer escalations inbound via support. Assigning incident lead to myself.

emily (support-L2): A few customers reported timeouts and 502s. Example request_id=rn-0a1b2c3d, user-org=AcmeAI, started seeing errors ~09:22Z. Repro steps from their side: curl with streaming body hangs then 504. They sent trace: gateway->runtime handshake timeout.

ajay (infra): Looking at gateway logs — rate of upstream resets jumped. snippet: 
```
2024-12-03T09:23:12Z gateway INFO upstream_reset: conn_reset id=rn-0a1b2c3d upstream=runtime-usw2a reason=RST
2024-12-03T09:23:19Z gateway WARN 502 response id=rn-0a1b2c3f latency=1204ms
2024-12-03T09:24:01Z gateway WARN 504 response id=rn-0a1b2c4a latency=3002ms
```

ajay (infra): p50 latency for inference generation increased from 180ms->450ms in the affected zones, p95 up to 2.3s. Runtime containers look healthy, GPU usage normal. Not CPU/GPU saturation.

neteng (carrier-team): We see transient BGP flap events on the transit session to TransitX peering at 13:23Z and 13:25Z (provider logs). syslog sample: 
```
Dec 03 13:23:02 leaf-agg kernel: BGP session reset with TransitX, reason=hold-time expired
Dec 03 13:23:02 leaf-agg bgp[2345]: peer 203.0.113.7 down: holdtime expired
Dec 03 13:25:10 leaf-agg bgp[2345]: peer 203.0.113.7 established
```

neteng (carrier-team): Running tcpdump on egress and see microburst drops -- short bursts of packet loss (~5-8% over ~10s windows) on the aggregation links to TransitX. Dump shows many retransmits and duplicated packets.

ops-bot: Attached alert graph: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1791209876 (image)

sophia (oncall): Sounds like cross-zone networking blips rather than runtime. Plan: 1) activate smart-routing fallback for requests originating to affected AZs (fail traffic to us-west-2c) 2) increase gateway upstream timeout + retries for 15m 3) open TAC with TransitX (neteng did) and escalate to severity 1 if they can't confirm mitigation.

devex: For customers doing streaming, we should provide a repro snippet they can use while we investigate: 
```
# reproducible curl that shows 504 from gateway
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"stream test\n"}' --max-time 20
```

emily (support-L2): Shared repro snippet with AcmeAI and asked for syslogs + request ids. Also opened support ticket: SUP-4472. They confirmed they see packet drops in traceroute to our egress IPs.

neteng (carrier-team): TAC opened with TransitX: TAC-81234. They confirm intermittent microbursts at their peering aggregation; their suggested mitigation is to shift a subset of prefixes to alternate path and patch aggregation switch buffer behavior. They've scheduled a maintenance change at +45m to apply a firmware fix.

ajay (infra): Implemented temporary rule: prefer us-west-2c endpoints for gateway routing for 10m and enabled retries=3, per-request backoff on 502/504. Also enabled prefix-level health checks to avoid sending traffic to nodes showing upstream RSTs. Rolling this in now.

sophia (oncall): Rolling update applied at 09:33Z. Early signs: 5xx rate dropped from 8.7% -> 1.9% over first 5m post-mitigation. p95 latency trending down but still above baseline.

billing: We have two enterprise customers impacted with SLA clauses. They requested temporary credit for the window if we exceed 0.5% error rate for >1h. Please keep Billing looped.

emily (support-L2): Notifying impacted customers with concise incident note and mitigation steps. Asking if we should provide a fallback region guide for customers (suggest enabling multi-region endpoint).

neteng (carrier-team): After TransitX fix (applied at 10:15Z), we saw BGP stability return and burst drops disappear. Captured pcap and forwarded to TransitX for postmortem. They assigned internal change id CX-4511.

sophia (oncall): Confirming final state at 10:20Z: error rate back to ~0.3%, latency within normal variance. Closing active mitigation. Will schedule formal postmortem.

devex: Follow-up action: add a short note to docs about recommended client-side retries/backoff and multi-region design patterns for low-latency workloads. I'll draft.

ajay (infra): Action items (quick): 1) collect full gateway + runtime logs for 09:20-10:20Z (ajay) 2) pcap + tcpdump + BGP logs upload to incident bucket (neteng) 3) customer impact list + support artifacts (emily) 4) coordinate billing notes (billing) 5) RCA meeting tomorrow 14:00Z (sophia)

sophia (oncall): Adding followup: review smart-routing fallback thresholds to make them more aggressive for streaming workloads. Also consider probing TransitX alternate paths earlier.

emily (support-L2): Customers updated. They appreciated the quick reroute. Keeping SUP-4472 and TAC-81234 linked.

ops-bot: Incident resolved. Summary: root cause = TransitX peering microbursts causing transient packet loss and BGP resets. Impact = elevated 5xx/timeouts for hosted inference in us-west zones (us-west-2a/2b) for ~55m. Mitigation = smart-route failover to us-west-2c + provider firmware patch. Postmortem scheduled.

sophia (oncall): Thanks team. If anyone still has files to upload to the incident folder, please do so. I'll kick off the postmortem doc and invite relevant folks. :thumbsup:
